analysis.title: Calm before the storm, or before the deal? + Energy Daily 06/11/26
key_insights: Brent is on track to finish the week about 15% lower on renewed hopes of a diplomatic resolution to the US-Iran conflict. The UBS energy specialist salesperson (Dominic Ellis) says the market is pricing in de-escalation without evidence of real progress.

Reuters reports Iran sent the US a nuclear proposal via Qatari mediators. Iran says it will be discussed only after the US meets seven conditions, and Iran's top security official said that until then it will neither open the Strait of Hormuz nor negotiate.

Iran's seven demands: lift sanctions, release frozen funds, end the US naval blockade of Iranian vessels, guarantees against renewed US and Israeli attacks and an end to attacks on Iranian allies, withdraw US forces from the region, pay reparations, and accept Iranian control of the Strait of Hormuz (possibly with transit tolls).

Ellis finds it hard to imagine major US concessions on any of the seven points, even if they are a maximalist opening stance. He sees a return to military conflict as far more likely than diplomatic progress, which would risk further damage to regional energy production and export infrastructure.

Several brokers argue that demand destruction from high oil prices and refining margins pushed the global oil market into surplus in October. Ellis says this is not supported by the most recent data he has seen and is waiting for a full UBS energy macro update.
EU integrated oil companies imply about $70/b oil. Ellis sees considerable room for further correction in oil before valuation becomes challenging for the sector.

US equities had their biggest selloff since Covid on Thursday. The Nasdaq closed -6.36% and the S&P 500 -4.36%, wiping $2.3T of market cap from US tech. SOX fell 12%, and Autos & Software fell 4%, Consumer Discretionary & Retail 3% and Financials 3%.

The selloff began as AI-led selling and broadened into a positioning unwind. Concern about a slowdown in AI build-out is starting to be read as a risk to the wider economy. Press reports say Microsoft is tightening scrutiny of projects and weighing whether to strike new neocloud deals.
Risk-off cross-asset moves: US Treasuries rallied with the curve flattening, gold +1% and WTI +3%.

Overnight Asia followed: Nikkei -6%, Kospi -5%, TWSE -3.75%, CSI 300 -1.5%, Hang Seng -1.25%. Eurostoxx futures were down 1% early, and NDX futures bounced 1% off the lows, a tentative sign of dip buying.

The UBS US strategy team flags possible further retail selling into the weekend, and Risk Control Funds needing to sell $100B on Friday. The desk expects the short leg that rallied on the unwind against AI to give back gains into the weekend.

UBS expects a slightly better than consensus October jobs report: NFP +65k, private payrolls +70k, unemployment dipping to 4.14%. UBS views the firmer print as largely technical, driven by seasonal flows rather than improving labour demand.

Political backdrop: Republicans lost heavily in the midterms. Bloomberg reports Secretary of State Rubio is weighing leaving the administration (he denied it to the NYT). Defense Secretary Hegseth vowed to fight impeachment efforts and defended the Iran war, which the desk says could support oil after the market rallied on peace hopes post-midterms.

MOL 3Q26 CCS EBITDA was HUF555bn ($1,760m), in line with company-compiled consensus of HUF553bn and 6% above UBSe of HUF523bn. Net income was HUF252bn, 1% below consensus and below UBSe of HUF290bn on a higher effective tax rate (29% vs 17% UBSe).

Orlen 3Q EBITDA (LIFO) excluding impairments was PLN14.8bn, 3% below consensus and UBSe at PLN15.2bn. Reported net income of PLN5.6bn missed consensus of PLN7.3bn and UBSe of PLN7.7bn on a 40% effective tax rate and PLN1.8bn of impairments. A working capital build of PLN4.4bn vs a UBSe release of PLN0.9bn offset stronger underlying cash flow.
China's state refiners are expected to cut diesel exports in November on tight inventories. Energy Aspects trimmed its November diesel export forecast by 400,000 tons to 580,000 tons.

Ukraine's renewed drone attacks hit Russian refineries (Ryazan, after Yaroslavl earlier in the week), ending a pause in strikes and worsening Russian diesel shortages while Russia exports diesel under a deal with the US.

US upstream M&A value reached $12.6B in 3Q (vs $11.5B in 2Q) per Enverus, with a surge in October including EQT acquiring Range Resources for $13.8B and Crescent Energy buying Devon's Eagle Ford assets for $4.2B. 2026 year-to-date deal value of $80.5B already exceeds last year's total.

UBS research flow shows a 3Q26 beat from COP, EOG, TRP (with raised guidance), TRGP (beat, raise, 2027 dividend hike) and CNQ. LBRT is down more than 20% since the midterms and SM Energy sold off sharply on Uinta takeaway constraints.

earnings_insights: MOL 3Q26: CCS EBITDA HUF555bn ($1,760m) vs company-compiled consensus HUF553bn and UBSe HUF523bn (reported 11/5-11/6). Net income HUF252bn vs consensus HUF255bn and UBSe HUF290bn. Two positive one-offs (about $100m insurance compensation after the Danube fire, about $133m from dissolving the foundation) were already in consensus and UBSe.

Orlen 3Q26: EBITDA (LIFO) excluding impairments PLN14.8bn vs company-compiled consensus (3% above the print) and UBSe PLN15.2bn. Reported net income PLN5.6bn vs consensus PLN7.3bn and UBSe PLN7.7bn. CFFO (UBS calculation) PLN12.2bn vs UBSe PLN12.8bn. Underlying cash flow excluding working capital PLN16.6bn vs UBSe PLN11.9bn, offset by a working capital build of PLN4.4bn vs a UBSe release of PLN0.9bn.

ONGC Q2FY27 (reported): EBITDA in line with UBSe and consensus. Production in line with UBSe (oil -5% y/y, -1% q/q; gas -2% y/y, +2% q/q). Sales 3% below UBSe. Interim dividend Rs8/share. High dividend income and high impairment affected profit after tax.
LG Chemical 3Q (reported): operating profit missed UBSe on petrochemical losses, and non-operating items drove the net loss.
PetroReconcavo 3Q26 (reported): EBITDA 7% above UBSe and 3% above consensus, with FCF equity yield of 4.0% (post-WK) or 7.6% (ex-WK).
COP, EOG, TRP, TRGP, CNQ, MUR reported 3Q26 beats per UBS research headlines. TRP raised guidance and TRGP raised its 2027 dividend. EOG's beat came with a new JKM-linked gas sales agreement.
Mahanagar Gas: UBS sees volume outlook intact at 8-10%, with higher gas costs pressuring near-term margins.

geopolitical: Iran sent the US a nuclear proposal via Qatar. Iran says it will be discussed only after the US meets seven conditions, and that it will neither open the Strait of Hormuz nor negotiate until then.

Iran's seven conditions include lifting sanctions, releasing frozen funds, ending the US naval blockade of Iranian vessels, guarantees against renewed US and Israeli attacks, a US force withdrawal from the region, reparations and recognition of Iranian control of the Strait of Hormuz (possibly with tolls).
Trump declined on Tuesday to rule out resuming combat operations after the US midterms, and Iran plans wider retaliation if war resumes.

Hegseth defended the Iran war as 'courageous and historic' after voters punished Republicans in the midterms. Bloomberg reports Rubio is weighing leaving the administration, which he denied to the NYT.
Trump predicted a 'big agreement' that is 'going to involve more than Ukraine' and 'might involve all of Europe' (Bloomberg).

Ukraine renewed drone strikes on Russian refineries (Ryazan, Yaroslavl), ending a pause in strikes and worsening Russian fuel shortages while Russia ships diesel abroad under an export deal with Trump.
Zelenskiy asked the Ibero-American Summit in Madrid for energy infrastructure aid, saying Russia has damaged every power plant in Ukraine.

tension_points.bull_case: Iran sent a nuclear proposal via Qatar and the post-midterm political shock may have raised the US administration's willingness to negotiate. Oil fell about 15% on the week on hopes of reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
tension_points.bear_case: Iran says it will neither negotiate nor open the Strait until the US meets seven conditions, which UBS's Ellis thinks the US is very unlikely to accept. He sees a return to military conflict as far more likely, with risk to regional energy infrastructure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Iran's proposal being discussed only after the US meets the seven demands. If the US does not move on them, the de-escalation pricing fails. The report gives no specific price level.
